display.title: Episode 217: The Return of Little Tzip Tzip (Before Purim)
display.summary_short: A week before Purim: a 'My Sefer Torah' contest entry, a fourth-grade class says the Shema, the parable of the little bird who smelled dirt everywhere, and a guide to the mitzvos of Purim.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week before Purim, in Adar Sheini. Uncle Yossi describes a colorful entry in the 'My Sefer Torah' drawing contest, decorated with a Torah crown and the verse from Tehillim that the Torah is better than thousands of gold and silver pieces, and reminds listeners about the newsletter and joining Tzivos Hashem. After the Hakochainik march, a fourth-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema. Story time: little Tzip Tzip, a baby bird, flies east, west, north and south and comes home each time complaining of a bad smell, until her mother finds a speck of dirt on the tip of her own nose. Uncle Yossi explains the lesson: look at others with a good eye; as the Baal Shem Tov taught, a fault we see in someone else is like a mirror, and the Sages say to correct ourselves first. After a sponsor message, he goes through Taanis Esther, the Megillah, tzedakah for the poor, the gragger, mishloach manos and the Purim seudah, and invites everyone to the Purim night program.
display.lesson: Look at others with a good eye and correct your own faults first; the faults we see in others are often our own.
